restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages 0^32 || x and 0^32 || y (x != y, 256-bit little-endian integers): one chunk of one block, chaining value IV, counter 0, length 64, flags 11 (CHUNK_START|CHUNK_END|ROOT), 3 rounds, unkeyed, the complete 256-bit digest (blake3-r3-prefix-v1). They are found as a collision g(x) = g(y) of the walk g(x) = f(x) XOR q, f(x) = digest(0^32 || x), q a fixed 256-bit mask (the polarities of the digest planes of the generated circuit); g(x) = g(y) iff f(x) = f(y). Plain birthday search; no differential or structural property of the 3 rounds is used.

Machine, a declared convention of this entry (H3, supporting): a classical load/store machine with 256-bit words, 256-bit immediates and 800 registers under collision-frontier-v5 (the profile fixes the word size and charges loads and stores, not a register count); 638 operations (C of blake3-r3) to the unit. Charged: every add, AND, OR, XOR, shift, compare, branch, register move, load, store and the random word. The main loop evaluates 256 trails bit-sliced with pivot full adders: 17275 operations per batch (17238 gates, a 34-operation stage-1 test, 3 loop operations), no load, store or move, no complement operation; it needs 771 registers. Code: 5 bytes per register-only gate (40-bit word), 36 bytes per other instruction (proof.md 3.1). Smaller files are priced in proof.md 3.5.

time_log2 is an upper bound: every term of proof.md Section 3.4 is enforced by a halt of the program (B batches, e2max stage-1 hits, 87359 table keys, 1 cut trail, a recovery of two passes of at most c + 2^48 batches each, one recovery), and the bound charges each at its limit. The attempt is single: one fresh uniform 256-bit word r, no restart, no amplification, no stored collision, no advice; m0..m7 = 0. Distinguished points: low 32 bits zero and the next 90 bits below 1328 (density 1328 / 2^122). The generator that builds the circuit at setup is charged (17,583,600 operations).

Memory: 87359 table entries of 10 bytes (873590 bytes) plus 132935 bytes of code (17875 gate words of 5 bytes and 1210 other instructions of 36 bytes) plus 16,384 bytes of counters and the plane copy plus 25,600 bytes for the 800 registers: 1048509 bytes = 2^19.99991; claimed as 20, the log2 of the 2^20-byte budget (the scalar policy adds 0 to time_log2). The circuit generator that runs at setup is a two-pass C program charged at 1445 compiled instructions (52020 bytes) and 22012 bytes of scratch, held in the region that the table and the register file occupy once the search runs: setup phase 223351 bytes, search phase 1048509 (proof 3.6). It was run in a sandbox capped at 1,048,576 bytes of guest memory and as a native binary with its address space capped at 2^20 bytes; both emit the identical program.

Success probability at least 0.39: Lemma 2 of proof.md Section 4 proves it for a uniformly random function from the lazy-sampling hazard (the first collision of the run and the detection delay, no conditioning on which trails finish, the cut count bounded by a proved theorem; bound 0.39000, exact certificate in Appendix A, none spare); H1, score-critical (clauses (a) to (d), declared and not proved), says the real attempt succeeds at least as often. Nothing else in the bound is heuristic. If the hazard were (1 - eps) / N the plan needs extra time: 0.0073 bit for eps = 0.01, 0.0370 bit for eps = 0.05, 0.0760 bit for eps = 0.10, 0.2075 bit for eps = 0.25.

The declared experiments run this program in the organizer sandbox: bsrho-n18 (one attempt of the 256-lane search per trial at width 18, DP = low 2 bits zero) and proj-k0-w256 (2048 points of the target at width 256 per trial, a pair when two digests agree in the low 21 bits). Each returns pairs whose complete 3-round digests agree in the stated low bits. They are program checks: no number of the claim is estimated from their counts and no sampling premise is used. No outside code or library is used.

No nonuniform advice and no prefix: the mask q is derived by the generator. Credited derivative: our own 62cfd777 (B3R3PV, blake3 round 3, 124.8123, passed the judges: the program), eaef120f (B3R4f, the same program at 4 rounds with the first-collision proof of Section 4), 0ecdfe35 (B3R4u5b, the 5-byte rows with the 17-bit trail number), a6ee439c, 9f69f1cc, 41b32afc, 75d5e1f9, 0a9640ed and 3356413f (program, search, ledger, register convention), 616120b2 (the 5-byte gate encoding, re-implemented from its text; no file used or run), and jungjipdo's 6ae36351 for the pivot full adder and the mask walk g = f XOR q (re-implemented from its proof text; no file of it used or run). preprocessing_log2 = 14.9 is the setup and generator row, which is also inside time_log2.

heuristics.statement: Model premise, four clauses. Let F be a uniformly random function from 256-bit values to 256-bit values. For the fixed target, the probability that the single attempt of the search succeeds, with the walk g(x) = f(x) XOR q (f(x) = the complete 4-round digest of the 64-byte message 0^32 || x, q the fixed digest-plane mask of the generated circuit), is at least the probability P_F, over the fresh word r and a uniformly random F, that the same search succeeds when every evaluation of g is replaced by F (lazy sampling). Clauses: (a) distinct evaluated inputs collide with probability 2^-256, uniform and independent outputs; (b) the iterates from r + t have the first-collision law of a random mapping; (c) a point is a distinguished point (low 32 bits zero and the next 90 bits below 1328) with probability 1328 / 2^122, independently of the collision events; (d) adaptivity: the program chooses its points, and which trails finish, are cut or abort, from earlier outputs of g; given the whole history of the run and which later outputs are distinguished points, a fresh evaluation equals a given earlier non-distinguished output with probability at least 2^-256 (the lazy-sampling hazard of F). Proof.md Section 4 (Lemma 2) proves P_F >= 0.3900 for F from the hazard alone, from the first collision of the run and the detection delay (no conditioning on which trails finish, no fixed-size birthday step); (d) is the premise that g has that hazard. This is a comparison of two success events, not a statement about the entropy of r. Nothing else in the success bound is heuristic.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target blake3-r3-prefix-v1 restricted to 64-byte messages 0^32 || x, the fixed mask q, the 2^128-scale evaluation of g along about 85100 trails of mean length 2^111.62 started from r + t, 256 trails at a time. Not claimed for other messages, other round counts, or evaluations beyond this scale.
heuristics.extrapolation: Declared and not proved: an assumption, no proof is known. The full 256-bit functional graph, trails longer than 2^40 and 2^128 evaluations cannot be observed. The organizer experiments bsrho-n18 and proj-k0-w256 run this program on the real target at reduced width (the search at width 18) and at full width for 2048 points with 21-bit projections; they are program checks, no number of the claim is estimated from their counts, and no sampling premise is used. Extrapolation from these sizes to width 256 and 2^128 evaluations is by the premise only. If the collision hazard is (1 - eps) / N instead of 1 / N (clause (d), or a deficit eps in clause (a)), the plan of this program needs, to restore 0.39: 0.0073 bit for eps = 0.01, 0.0370 bit for eps = 0.05, 0.0760 bit for eps = 0.10, 0.2075 bit for eps = 0.25.
heuristics.limitations: A model premise about one fixed function, not a theorem: on the target the run is a deterministic function of r. It cannot be tested at width 256; the experiments reach width 18 and 21-bit projections of 2048 points per trial and do not measure collision structure at 2^128 evaluations. The bound has no margin above 0.39 (B is the least multiple of 10^24 that reaches it), so any hazard deficit is repaired by extra time, priced above: 0.0073 bit for eps = 0.01 (Tp 1322); 0.0370 bit for eps = 0.05 (Tp 1295); 0.0760 bit for eps = 0.10 (Tp 1260); 0.2075 bit for eps = 0.25 (Tp 1150).

heuristics.statement: Declared machine convention of this entry (supporting; a convention, not a claim about the benchmark; the register-file convention of our 0a9640ed, which passed the judges, here with 800 registers). The cost model prices a 256-bit word RAM with loads and stores and fixes no register count; this entry declares R = 800 registers of 256 bits, counted as 25,600 bytes of memory, and charges every operation, load, store and register move. The main loop (one batch of 256 trails, 17275 operations: the 17238-operation generated step, a 34-operation stage-1 test and 3 loop operations) has no load, store or move because the generated line needs 771 registers (output plane j in the register of input plane j). The organizer's reference count C(r3) = 638 is used only as the unit. Code is memory and its format is not fixed by the cost model: a register-only gate (the step, the stage-1 test, the recovery circuit) is charged as one 40-bit instruction word of 5 bytes (8-bit opcode, three 10-bit register numbers), every other instruction 36 bytes (opcode, registers, inline 256-bit immediate), and the code of the circuit generator 36 bytes per instruction of its compiled form (1445 instructions, proof.md 3.1, 3.6).
heuristics.scope: The loop body of one batch of 256 lanes, its stage-1 test and the handlers; table accesses, recovery, events and setup are charged at the stated bounds including loads and stores of their words.
heuristics.extrapolation: A machine with fewer than 771 registers would add loads and stores to every batch; proof.md 3.5 gives the cost (time_log2 124.8359 with 512 registers). The claim assumes the declared 800.
heuristics.limitations: The benchmark profile does not fix a register count or an instruction set; the declaration is this entry's own. The count 17238 is produced by the generator in the program (a C port of it emits the identical program in a memory-capped sandbox, proof 3.6) and the register allocation by `allocate`; smaller files are priced by the program's Belady allocation of the straight line (an upper bound on what a better schedule needs).
